after.abstract: Background Timely identification of Barrett's esophagus (BE) is crucial for early esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) detection. Screening is recommended from age 50 in individuals with additional risk factors, but biological BE onset age remains unknown. Objective Estimate biological BE onset age and duration before clinical diagnosis (dwell time). Design We applied a BE epigenetic clock to 61 samples from 41 patients in a population-representative Northern Ireland cohort and 164 samples from 140 patients in an independent UK cohort. BE dwell times were compared between patients with concurrent dysplasia/EAC and age- and sex-matched non-dysplastic BE controls in these cross-sectional studies. In a longitudinal cohort, pre-progression biopsies from 31 future high-grade dysplasia (HGD)/EAC progressors were compared with 35 non-progressors. Results Median estimated BE onset ages in the cross-sectional cohorts were 29.5 (IQR=22.5-45.8) and 29.3 (IQR=20.4-39.0) years, respectively. These estimates were further supported by independent epidemiologic modeling of age-specific BE prevalence data from more than 70,000 BE cases. Estimated dwell times were longer in patients with concurrent dysplasia (median difference 14.3 years; p=0.0042) or EAC (12.5 years; p=0.0002) than matched non-dysplastic BE controls. Dwell time exceeding 19.8 years was associated with higher odds of HGD/EAC progression (OR=12.1, 95% CI 3.7-47.5; p=9.96 x 10-9;). Conclusion BE may arise decades before diagnosis. Although these findings do not justify lowering screening age, they suggest one-time screening from age 50 years may detect existing high-risk BE. Further modeling is warranted to evaluate implications for population-based screening, alongside prospective validation of epigenetic tissue age for progression risk stratification.

after.authors: Lan, Y.; Lin, C.; Liu, H.; Zhou, H.; Xie, B.; Chen, J.; Gao, H.; Zheng, Q.; Chen, Y.
after.author_corresponding_institution: The First Affiliated Hospital of Shantou University Medical College
after.abstract: Background: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome reflects shared pathophysiology across metabolic, renal and cardiovascular systems, yet circulating proteins with causal effects spanning multiple CKM domains remain unclear. We aimed to identify and prioritize cross-domain candidate proteins using an integrative, dual-platform plasma proteogenomic framework. Methods: We combined genetic causal inference, statistical colocalization, single-cell expression mapping, and structure-based druggability assessment. Cis-protein quantitative trait loci (cis-pQTL) instruments were derived from two independent plasma proteomic platforms, UKB-PPP (2,030 proteins with valid cis instruments) and deCODE (1,640 proteins). Genetic causal inference (two-sample Mendelian randomization) was performed against seven CKM-related outcomes across the metabolic (type 2 diabetes [T2D], body mass index [BMI]), renal (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR], chronic kidney disease) and cardiovascular (coronary artery disease, heart failure, stroke) domains. Proteins showing false discovery rate (FDR)-significant associations in at least two CKM domains independently on both platforms were prioritized, and cross-platform directional concordance was evaluated as a robustness measure. Prioritized proteins were followed by colocalization, and characterization using single-cell expression, disease-association and druggability resources. Structural and ligand-efficiency analyses were performed for the leading candidate using its co-crystallized inhibitor complex. Results: Proteome-wide analysis yielded 9,734 (UKB-PPP) and 8,837 (deCODE) protein-outcome estimates, with 77.9% two-platform directional concordance. Cross-domain prioritization identified six proteins (ARG1, GSTA1, INHBB, ITIH1, NCAN, SHBG), all acting across the metabolic-renal axis. Colocalization provided strong support for GSTA1 with eGFR (posterior probability of a shared causal variant 0.97) and ARG1 with BMI (0.93). Genetically higher GSTA1 was associated with lower eGFR and higher T2D risk, with kidney expression confined to proximal tubule cells. Genetically higher ARG1 was associated with lower BMI and lower T2D risk, consistent with hepatocyte-restricted expression. Both proteins were small-molecule tractable. For GSTA1, the inhibitor-bound structure (PDB 1GSF) showed a deep, enclosed H-site, and three chemotypes with previously reported low-micromolar potency against recombinant hGSTA1-1 (ethacrynic acid and the dietary flavonols fisetin and myricetin) all exceeded the lead-like ligand-efficiency threshold (0.30 kcal mol-1 per heavy atom). Conclusions: Using dual-platform proteogenomics, we identify genetically supported cross-metabolic-renal candidate proteins in CKM syndrome, with GSTA1 and ARG1 emerging as the most robust, pharmacologically tractable candidates. These findings nominate actionable targets and mechanistic entry points for CKM syndrome.

after.authors: Matoke-Muhia, D.; Tuluso, M.; Kimemia, B. B.; Osero, B.; Kamau, L.; Ndungu, J. M.; Ofwete, R.; Thiongo, K.; Maranga, D.
after.author_corresponding_institution: KEMRI Centre for Biotechnology Research and Development
after.abstract: Background Visceral Leishmaniasis (VL) is a neglected tropical disease (NTD) caused by Leishmania infantum and L. donovani and transmitted by an infectious bite of a female phlebotomine sandfly. The disease disproportionately affects impoverished and underserved populations, where inadequate access to healthcare. In Kenya, 11 out of the 47 counties are endemic for VL, a fatal disease if untreated. Parasitological methods remain the gold standard for diagnosing VL, however they are invasive and require specialised training and equipment. Serological tests such as Rapid Diagnostic Tests (RDTs) are widely used for screening but can still report positive results way after treatment due to persistence of anti-VL antibodies. It is recommended that VL diagnosis follows an algorithmic approach. This study evaluated diagnostic performance of rK28 and rK39 RDTs (Kala-azar Detect and IT Leish) in various algorithmic combinations against a composite reference standard. Methodology We evaluated rK28 and Kala-azar Detect along with rK39 IT-Leish as index tests, and Direct Agglutination Test (DAT) as the reference test. Participants were recruited from seven health facilities in Marsabit and Turkana counties. Blood samples were collected together with patient demographic data. Treatment followed the national algorithm and health facility routine procedures. Diagnostic test performance was assessed individually, in parallel, and sequential algorithmic combinations. Specificity, sensitivity, balanced accuracy, negative and positive predictive values were statistically estimated. Results A total of 398 participants were recruited, with most reported clinical symptoms being fever and splenomegaly. Individually, the rK28 kit demonstrated 96% sensitivity, 86% specificity, and 91.2% balanced accuracy (BA). The rK39 IT-Leish had 87% sensitivity, specificity 93%, and BA of 90.4%, while Kala-azar Detect had 67% sensitivity, 91% specificity and 79% BA. IT Leish to rK28 algorithm based on negatives had highest BA (90%), with 92% sensitivity and 88% specificity, while rK28 to Kala-azar detect algorithm based on positives showed the lowest BA (80%) with 65% sensitivity and 94.1% specificity. Discussion The rK28 RDT demonstrated high sensitivity (96-98%) and moderate specificity (72-86%), findings broadly consistent with reports elsewhere. In contrast, the rK39-based tests showed higher specificity (91-93%) but lower sensitivity (67-87%), limiting their effectiveness in elimination programs. Parallel testing algorithms combining rK28 and rK39 RDTs improved sensitivity up to 97.7%, whereas sequential approaches increased specificity at the expense of sensitivity when compared to rK28 alone. These approaches were more balanced as compared to sequential which increased overall specificity and reduced sensitivity. This flexibility in combinations provides more options for elimination programs. The performance of rK28 gives it an advantage over rK39 kits, especially with IT Leish facing stockouts. While the study faced limitations including lack of PCR data leading to reliance on DAT as the reference standard, and underpowered secondary analyses, the findings provide strong preliminary evidence guiding national algorithm, supply chain, and policy decisions that may accelerate VL elimination. Conclusion The findings demonstrate that diagnostic algorithms incorporating rK28 provide robust performance for VL diagnosis. They support consideration of rK28 diagnostic kit for VL diagnostic algorithms enhancing case detection for control and elimination efforts in Eastern Africa

after.authors: Hu, Z.; Ye, J.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Critical Care Medicine, The First Affiliated Hospital of Ningbo University, China
after.category: intensive care and critical care medicine
after.abstract: Abstract Background & Aims. The 2026 unified definition of acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) requires bilirubin [≥]5 mg/dL and INR [≥]1.5 before extrahepatic organ involvement is graded. Many critically ill patients with cirrhosis have extrahepatic organ failure without such liver failure. How the unified grade classifies them is unknown. Methods.We applied the unified, EASL-CLIF and NACSELD classifications around intensive care unit (ICU) admission to adults with cirrhosis in MIMIC-IV, excluding prior or perioperative liver transplantation. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality; in-hospital mortality was examined in eICU. Results. Among 2,972 patients, 33.8% met ACLF criteria by the unified grade, 65.2% by EASL-CLIF and 29.9% by NACSELD. Of EASL-CLIF-positive patients, 1,086 (56.0%) were assigned unified grade 0; 54.7% of them were ventilated, 48.7% received vasopressors, and their 28-day mortality was 32.6% (95% CI, 29.9% to 35.4%), versus 11.8% in patients negative by both definitions. Patients with unified grade 0 accounted for 46.7% of all 28-day deaths. The unified grade discriminated 28-day mortality less well than EASL-CLIF grade (difference in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC], -0.071; 95% CI, -0.090 to -0.050) and the CLIF-C OF score (-0.105; -0.123 to -0.088). Among 1,883 patients with coded decompensation, 45.8% of those EASL-CLIF-positive were assigned grade 0, with 28-day mortality of 34.3%. In eICU, in-hospital mortality was 28.9% among patients positive by EASL-CLIF alone. Conclusions. In critically ill patients with cirrhosis, the unified grade assigned grade 0 to about half of those meeting EASL-CLIF criteria, and one in three of them died within 28 days. In the ICU, unified grade 0 should not be read as low risk. ACLF types A and B could not be determined.

after.abstract: Background: Sublingual buprenorphine (SLB) is commonly prescribed to treat opioid use disorder. Pharmacoepidemiologic studies suggest an association between SLB and severe dental caries, yet clinical investigations are lacking. Objective: To assess caries experience and caries-related risk factors among patients taking SLB. Methods: This pilot cross-sectional study enrolled 11 subjects taking SLB films, 10 taking SLB tablets, and 10 age- and sex-matched controls. Demographic, medical, dental, and behavioral data were collected. Caries examinations were performed. Salivary pH, buffering capacity, and flow rate were measured. Saliva and plaque levels of Mutans streptococci and Candida spp. were determined. Oral pH dynamics and salivary concentrations of buprenorphine, its metabolites, and naloxone were monitored. Results: Caries experience was greater in SLB subjects than controls and higher among tablet versus film subjects (p<0.05). SLB subjects exhibited lower salivary pH and buffering capacity (p<0.05), and elevated salivary levels of Mutans streptococci (p<0.05) and Candida spp. (p<0.001). SLB administration was associated with rapid oral acidification and prolonged recovery. Salivary buprenorphine exposure was elevated and correlated with baseline pH (p<0.01), suggesting ion trapping contributes to oral retention. Conclusion: Patients receiving SLB exhibit increased caries experience likely resulting from localized acidification favoring caries-associated microorganisms and prolonged oral exposure to buprenorphine.

after.authors: Grant, A. D.; Prideaux, C. S.; Rosales, M.; Capano-Wehrle, L.; Moos, J.; Mkrtytchian, N.; Luna, V.; Krupa, M. C. E.; Craft, N.

after.abstract: Background. Upper respiratory infections are common and carry a greater burden in older adults. IDP (Immune Defense Protein) is a dietary supplement whose active ingredient is a complex of milk-derived bioactive whey proteins. Prior studies of IDP report enhanced antibody response following influenza vaccination, suggesting a potential for reduction of incidence, duration, and severity of upper respiratory symptoms. This study evaluated the effects of IDP supplementation on the incidence, type, duration, and severity of upper respiratory symptoms in older adults during cold and flu season, along with rescue medication use and quality of life. Methods. This was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study with three arms (placebo, standard dose of 50mg IDP /day, and advanced dose of 200mg IDP /day). Participants completed a one-week baseline period followed by a 16-week product use period, reporting daily upper respiratory symptoms via the Wisconsin Upper Respiratory Symptom Survey (WURSS-24). Participants additionally logged quality of life using the Short Form 36 (SF-36). ANCOVA for change from baseline, mixed models for repeated measures (MRMM), as well as Kruskal Wallis (KW) tests of area under the curve of symptom frequency and severity were used to compare trajectories over time. Results. N=255 participants (n=88 Placebo, n=85 50 mg IDP , n=82 200 mg IDP ) were evaluated. Analysis of individual symptom trends over time revealed that chest congestion and cough decreased in severity and duration significantly faster in the 50 mg IDP and 200 mg IDP groups compared to Placebo (KW for Area Under the Curve p<0.05). ANCOVA of baseline to Week-16 change and MRMM of total WURSS-24 symptom frequency, severity and rescue medication use revealed no significant difference between arms (ANCOVA and MRMM p > 0.05). SF-36 quality of life did not differ between arms. Adverse events potentially attributable to product use were infrequent, resolved, and did not differ between arms. Conclusions. Sixteen weeks of daily IDP supplementation was associated with a reduction in duration and severity of cough and chest congestion in older adults. IDP appears safe and tolerable.

after.author_corresponding_institution: Institute of Cardiovascular Science, University College London, London, UK
after.abstract: Background: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is characterized by abnormal dilation and functional remodelling of the thoracic aorta. Current detection and surveillance rely largely on imaging, limiting population-wide risk stratification. Circulating proteins may provide biological insight into aortic remodelling and support future biomarker development. We aimed to identify circulating proteomic patterns associated with imaging-derived thoracic aortic diameter and aortic stiffness in a large population-based cohort. Methods: A proteome-wide association study was conducted in 6773 UK Biobank participants with available plasma proteomic and cardiac imaging data. A combined thoracic aortic diameter was derived from taking the maximum of standardized ascending and descending measurements, while stiffness was derived using a pressure-free index of aortic wall properties. Associations with 2920 circulating proteins were evaluated using multivariable linear regression with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Functional enrichment analysis was performed using the complete ranked protein list across Hallmark, curated, and Gene Ontology Biological Process collections. Principal component analysis (PCA) was performed as a secondary analysis to explore shared and divergent variation between the two phenotypes. Results: In age- and sex-adjusted analyses, 358 proteins were associated with aortic diameter and 60 with stiffness after FDR correction. Sequential adjustment materially altered these associations; in the primary fully adjusted models, 417 proteins were associated with diameter and six with stiffness. Functional enrichment analyses highlighted complement/coagulation, extracellular matrix organization, and contractile pathways associated with aortic diameter. In contrast, although only a few individual proteins were associated with stiffness, rank-based pathway analysis across the full proteome identified a distinct enrichment pattern involving cytokine signalling, protein processing, and intracellular transport. Aortic diameter and stiffness were only modestly correlated (r = 0.21). Secondary PCA showed that the first principal component (PC1) largely overlapped with the diameter-associated profile, with 310 of 370 PC1-associated proteins also associated with diameter. Four proteins (REN, BCAN, GGH and THY1) were associated with both diameter and stiffness in addition to being associated with PC1. Conclusion: Circulating proteomic profiling identified markedly different and minimally overlapping molecular patterns associated with thoracic aortic diameter and stiffness. Structural dilation was primarily linked to complement/coagulation, extracellular matrix, and contractile pathways, whereas stiffness reflected a smaller, more distinct aspect of aortic remodelling involving cytokine signalling and cellular transport processes. The four shared proteins across both phenotypes (REN, BCAN, GGH and THY1) represent candidates for further biomarker and causal investigation.

after.title: Preprint: Reconstructing the range-normalized terminal QRS from V1 and V6 using the time-embedded 3D ECG
after.authors: Bermejo Valdes, A. J.; Archer Jimenez, J.
after.author_corresponding_institution: 061 Emergency Medical Services Department, La Rioja Health Service
after.abstract: Objective. Can a fixed V1/V6 projection of the time-embedded 3D ECG estimate the final 40 ms of V2-V5 more accurately than a fitted single lead? Methods. We used simultaneous recordings from the Lobachevsky University Electrocardiography Database (LUDB), with cardiologist-annotated QRS complexes in all six chest leads. We fitted both models in 118 patients and tested them in 80 others. Root mean squared error (RMSE) is expressed in percentage points (pp) of the target lead's 10-second amplitude range. Results. In 733 test beats, patient-weighted terminal RMSE fell from 12.58 to 10.64 pp (difference 1.94 pp, 95% bootstrap confidence interval 1.30 to 2.55). Reductions were 3.23, 2.85 and 1.35 pp in V3, V4 and V5. In V2 the difference was 0.35 pp (95% interval -0.35 to 1.05). In 702 matched beats from 77 patients, the overall advantage was 2.22 pp at the automatic V1/V6 end and 1.92 pp at the annotated target end. Of 1,498 beat-lead pairs with whole-QRS correlation of at least 0.95, 28.84% still had terminal RMSE of at least 10 pp. Conclusions. A fixed V1/V6 projection improved offline estimates of relative terminal amplitude in V3-V5 without fitting the target lead in the new patient. The gain was largest in V3 and V4 and uncertain in V2. Whether a reconstructed trace preserves a clinically recognizable notch or slur remains untested.

after.authors: Gellrich, F. F.; Kistner, A.; Guenther, C.; Hufnagel, C.; Hobelsberger, S.; Laske, J.; Beissert, S.; Aust, D.; Baretton, G.; Reidow, N.; Sergon, M.; Kather, J. N.; Ghaffari Laleh, N.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Dermatology, Faculty of Medicine and University Hospital Carl Gustav Carus, Technische Universitaet Dresden, Dresden, Germany
after.abstract: Background: The histopathological diagnosis of challenging melanocytic lesions remains limited by substantial interobserver variability. Although computational pathology foundation models demonstrated promising diagnostic performance, their predictions are often difficult to interpret in terms of established criteria. Objective: We evaluated a diagnostic framework combining foundation-model-based whole-slide image analysis, automated prediction of morphological features, and manually assessed PRAME immunohistochemistry. Methods: Using the Virchow2 foundation model and STAMP framework, we analyzed a retrospective cohort of 1,000 melanocytic lesions undergoing PRAME immunohistochemistry. Models were trained on 800 cases and evaluated on a temporally held-out test cohort of 200 cases. Results: The slide-level malignancy classifier achieved a test AUROC of 0.970 (AUPRC 0.984). Separate models predicted established histopathological criteria with high discrimination, including ulceration (AUROC 0.991) and dermal mitoses (AUROC 0.966). In contrast, predicting PRAME expression from H&E images alone showed lower performance (AUROC 0.776-0.780 for PRAME scores 4 and 0). An integrated model combining the slide-level malignancy score, AI-predicted morphological features, and manual PRAME status achieved an AUROC of 0.972 (AUPRC 0.975), comparable to the standalone classifier. In multivariable analysis, PRAME score 4 versus 0 was strongly associated with malignancy (adjusted OR 35.04, 95% CI 17.39-74.62). Conclusions: These findings demonstrate the feasibility of combining foundation-model-based histopathological analysis with established morphological criteria and PRAME immunohistochemistry. Although the integrated framework did not substantially improve overall discrimination, it provides a structured approach for incorporating complementary histopathological and immunohistochemical information into AI-assisted assessment of melanocytic lesions.

after.title: Preprint: Beyond National Averages: Social Contact Patterns in the Upper Midwest
after.authors: Dorelien, A.; Carlson, M.; Wheatley, M. M.; Erickson, L.; Morris, K.; Sweet, K.; Enns, E.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Washington
after.abstract: Background: Social contact surveys measure how individuals interact with each other, which directly influences disease transmission dynamics. The COVID-19 pandemic substantially altered how people live and work, highlighting the need for up-to-date and sub-national estimates of social contact patterns to inform disease modeling and public health planning. Methods: The Midwest Analytics & Disease Modeling Center (MADMC) conducted an opt-in social contact survey of upper Midwest residents, with about 60% of participants drawn from Minnesota. Participants reported all interpersonal contacts during the previous day, including the age of their contacts allowing for the analysis of mixing patterns. Detailed demographic information about the participants was also collected, allowing for additional subgroup analyses of contact patterns. Results: Participants in our sample had an average of 6.8 contacts per day (IQR: 2.0 - 8.0), which is within the range of recent post-pandemic US national and European estimates. Contacts varied across demographic groups, with those attending work or school in-person reporting the highest number of contacts. Mixing across most age group pairs was a little lower than in comparable national survey except for younger age groups, who had substantially higher rates of contact with same-age peers. Differences in the contact matrices alone were associated with a 6.7% difference in estimated basic reproduction number(R0). Near the epidemic threshold, even this modest difference could meaningfully affect transmission dynamics. These effects may be amplified or attenuated by pathogen-specific age patterns of susceptibility and infectiousness, leading to larger or smaller differences in R0 estimates derived from national versus regional mixing patterns. Conclusions: These findings provide empirical evidence on post-pandemic social contact patterns in the United States and highlight the potential implications of regional variation in social mixing for infectious disease transmission. The mean 6.8 daily contacts is consistent with evidence of persistent changes in daily routines following the pandemic. Incorporating contemporary, region-specific contact patterns into transmission models may improve their ability to capture geographic variation in transmission risk and inform epidemic forecasting.

after.authors: Wang, Z.; Hrytsenko, Y.; Almogy, S.; Spitzer, B. W.; Purushotham, Y.; Taylor, K.; Lin, H. J. J.; Tahir, U. A.; Raffield, L. M.; Rich, S.; Rotter, J.; Chen, Z. Z.; Sofer, T.

after.abstract: Background: Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet the relative contributions of proteomic (ProtS), metabolomic (MetS), and polygenic risk scores (PRS) to incident hypertension risk remain incompletely characterized. Methods: We developed ProtS and MetS for systolic (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP), and hypertension using Elastic Net regression in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA). We incorporated these scores with previously developed BP PRSs into 5 incremental XGBoost models, with external validation in the Jackson Heart Study (JHS). We further applied transfer learning to adapt the MESA-derived models to JHS. Elastic Net selected proteins were prioritized using Mendelian randomization, colocalization, and functional analyses. Results: In MESA, model discrimination improved with the addition of omics scores, with the combined model achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.72 compared with 0.63 for the clinical baseline model. In JHS, ProtS showed the highest AUC of 0.68 and the smallest cross-cohort performance decline, compared to MetS and PRS. Incorporating measured SBP and DBP substantially improved discrimination, with the PRS+BP model achieving an AUC of 0.80 in MESA and the baseline+BP model achieving an AUC of 0.74 in JHS. Among JHS participants with normal baseline BP, ProtS provided the strongest discrimination among models without measured BP (AUC = 0.62), while PRS+BP model achieved an AUC of 0.69. Leaf-weight refreshing consistently improved calibration in JHS while preserving discrimination. Mendelian randomization identified 77 proteins associated with BP traits or hypertension, involved in vascular, inflammatory, renal, and natriuretic pathways. Conclusions: ProtS demonstrated superior predictive performance and cross-cohort transferability among the omics modalities evaluated, while measured BP remained the strongest predictors of incident hypertension. Proteomic and genetic information may provide complementary biological signals for identifying individuals at elevated hypertension risk, particularly before clinically elevated BP is detectable.

after.abstract: Importance: The 7-day cutoff separating acute symptomatic from unprovoked poststroke seizures guides epilepsy diagnosis and long-term antiseizure medication but is consensus based and unvalidated against recurrence risk by stroke subtype. Objective: To determine whether seizure recurrence risk changes abruptly at day 7 and how it varies with first-seizure timing by stroke subtype. Design, Setting, and Participants: This pooled analysis of individual participant data from 36 cohorts in 22 countries (inclusion, 1994-2025) included adults with a first seizure after ischemic stroke, intracerebral hemorrhage, aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, or cerebral venous thrombosis. Exposure: Days from stroke onset (or venous thrombosis diagnosis) to first seizure. Main Outcomes and Measures: The 10-year cumulative incidence of unprovoked seizure recurrence, with death as a competing event, from stabilized inverse probability of treatment-weighted Fine-Gray spline models. Risk zones were based on the likelihood of being helped vs harmed and the 60% epilepsy threshold of the International League Against Epilepsy. Results: Of 2434 individuals (median [IQR] age, 63 [49-75] years; 1181 [48.5%] female), 684 (28.1%) had a seizure recurrence. Risk changed gradually with first-seizure timing, without a day-7 transition; overall 10-year risk differed by subtype (cerebral venous thrombosis, 44%; intracerebral hemorrhage, 43%; ischemic stroke, 40%; subarachnoid hemorrhage, 35%; P < .001). At day 7, the 10-year risk was 24% (95% CI, 17%-32%) after ischemic stroke, 30% (95% CI, 22%-38%) after intracerebral hemorrhage, 41% (95% CI, 22%-53%) after subarachnoid hemorrhage, and 58% (95% CI, 44%-71%) after cerebral venous thrombosis. The 60% threshold was crossed from day 71 after ischemic stroke, day 41 after intracerebral hemorrhage, and day 9 after cerebral venous thrombosis; after subarachnoid hemorrhage, only seizures on days 2 to 3 exceeded it. Mortality was inversely related to recurrence risk. Of 800 first seizures after day 7 following ischemic stroke or intracerebral hemorrhage, which would qualify as epilepsy under current criteria, 335 (42%) had a recurrence risk below the 60% diagnostic threshold. Conclusions and Relevance: In this pooled analysis, seizure recurrence risk after stroke rose gradually, not abruptly at day 7, and differed by subtype. After external validation, subtype-specific risk zones could inform individualized decisions about long-term antiseizure medication.

after.title: Preprint: Inter-articulatory Timing of Vocalic Tongue Body and Jaw Movements across Talkers with Dysarthria due to Various Neurological Conditions
after.authors: Thies, T.; Dietrich, M. S.; Mefferd, A.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Neurology, Faculty of Medicine and University Hospital Cologne, University of Cologne, Cologne, Germany
after.abstract: Purpose: This study compared inter-articulatory timing patterns of the tongue and jaw across talkers with Parkinson's disease (PD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), Huntington's disease (HD), multiple sclerosis (MS), and neurotypical controls (CON) to identify disease-related differences. The study also explored if a talker's tongue body cycle duration, which serve as a proxy for a talker's habitual speech rate, or a talker's reliance on their jaw, as indicated by their jaw movement amplitude, could predict their inter-articulatory timing patterns. Method: Using three-dimensional electromagnetic articulography, the movements of the posterior tongue and jaw were examined in 24 talkers with PD, 19 talkers with ALS, 18 talkers with HD, 18 talkers with MS, and 34 CON during a sentence repetition task ('Buy Kaia a kite'). The tongue movement during the segment [kai] served as the reference signal (tongue body cycle) for which the phase angle of the jaw reaching the maximum opening position during [kai] was calculated. Tongue body cycle durations were measured as the time between the tongue body movement onset to the tongue body movement offset. The jaw opening amplitude was measured as the relative positional change from the jaw's maximum closing position associated with [k] to the jaw's maximal opening position at the onset of the diphthong [ai]. Results: A significant group effect was found for phase angles. Pairwise comparisons showed that talkers with ALS had significantly larger phase angles than talkers with PD, MS, HD, and CON, indicating a timing pattern where the tongue reached the target [a] earlier relative to the jaw. No significant differences were found for any other pairwise comparisons. Furthermore, no significant associations were found between tongue body cycle durations and phase angles. A significant association was found between jaw amplitudes and phase angles when considering all talkers [rS(110) = .253, p = .008] and when only considering talkers of the control group [r(34) = .361, p = .036]. Conclusions: Findings suggest that during the production of [kai], tongue-jaw timing patterns of talkers with ALS differ from those of talkers with PD, MS, HD, and CON with the tongue reaching the maximum opening position before the jaw while the opposite pattern was observed for talkers of the other groups. However, the variability in tongue body cycle duration did not significantly contribute to the variability in phase angles and the variability in jaw amplitudes only accounted for 6% of the variability in phase angles across all talkers. Future studies are needed to determine if the observed tongue-jaw timing pattern of talkers with ALS generalizes to other phonetic contexts and determine the underlying factors that contribute to the unique tongue-jaw timing patterns of talkers with ALS.

after.title: Preprint: Adrenergic nerve fibers are depleted in adenomyosis myometrium
after.authors: Chevalier, N. R.; Huon, E.; Segard, O.; Ouali, M.; Plancke, M.; Boer Wigman, C.; Savy, T.; Pujol, T.; Bourdoncle, P.; Dietrich, G.; Petit, E.; Abrahami, Y.; Kouby, J.; Adam, J.; Lamau, M.-C.; Abo, C.
after.author_corresponding_institution: CNRS
after.abstract: Objective: Uterine dyscontractility in adenomyosis and endometriosis is at the heart of pain symptoms and disease pathogenesis. To elucidate possible causes of dyscontractility, we examined the distribution of smooth muscle, blood vessel, collagen and nerve fibers in full-thickness, serosa-to-endometrium myometrium of adenomyosis patients versus control. Design: Retrospective study. Subjects: Uterine biopsies from patients who underwent hysterectomy for adenomyosis (n = 26) or other non-adenomyosis indications (n=22, mostly myomas). Main Outcome Measures: Density profiles along the serosa-to-endometrium axis of smooth muscle (SMA), endothelium (PECAM), general innervation (PGP9.5) and adrenergic innervation (TH) obtained by immunofluorescence, mosaic epifluorescence imaging and machine-learning assisted segmentation. Fibrous collagen type I&III was quantified by second-harmonic generation microscopy (SHG). Results: The density profiles of smooth muscle, endothelium, collagen and PGP9.5 were similar between both patient groups. Sympathetic adrenergic nerve fiber density radiated from the serosa inwards, with a continuously decreasing density from the outer to the inner myometrium. Adrenergic inhibitory nerve fibers were 4 times less dense in the inner myometrium of adenomyosis uteri compared to controls. Conclusion: The enrichment of inhibitory adrenergic nerve fibers in the outer vs inner myometrium provides a neuro-muscular mechanism by which contractions are restricted to the inner myometrium outside of pregnancy. The depletion of TH fibers in adenomyosis implies that a higher thickness of myometrium is involved in uterine contractions, thus explaining junctional zone thickening and dyscontractility in this pathology. This depletion may be due to defective post-pregnancy adrenergic re-innervation of the myometrium.

after.authors: Ng, J. Y.; Tan, J.; Adapa, K.; Gupta, P. K.; Gupta, M.; Li, S.; Mehta, D. H.; Ring, M.; Shridhar, M.; Souza, J. P.; Yoshino, T.; Lee, M. S.; Cramer, H.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Institute of General Practice and Interprofessional Care, University Hospital Tubingen, Tubingen, Germany; Robert Bosch Center for Integrative Medicine and Heal
after.abstract: Background: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) chatbots are being explored for their potential to support the peer review process by improving efficiency and analytical capacity. While early applications show promise, concerns regarding ethics, privacy, and research integrity remain, and their use within traditional, complementary, and integrative medicine (TCIM) remains underexplored. This study examines TCIM researchers' attitudes and perceptions regarding the use of GenAI chatbots in peer review through a large-scale international survey. Methods: Corresponding authors of TCIM-related publications indexed in Ovid MEDLINE were invited to participate in an online, anonymous, international cross-sectional survey distributed via SurveyMonkey. The questionnaire collected data on demographic characteristics, the perceived importance of GenAI in peer review, the likelihood of adoption, and the perceived benefits and concerns. Results: A total of 889 eligible respondents participated. Overall, 40.25% (n=285/708) reported a positive perception of GenAI in peer review, and 41.67% (n=295/708) considered it important to the field. 34.24% researchers reported being likely (n=253/739) or 18.27% (135/739) very likely (totaling 52.51%) to use GenAI in peer review, highlighting a gap between perceived importance and intended adoption. Identified benefits included improved efficiency (50.72%, n=350/690), reduced reviewer workload (51.16%, n=353/690), and generation of constructive feedback (46.30%, n=319/689), reflecting respondents selecting "agree." Concerns included bias (49.85%, n=333/668), lack of transparency (42.86%, n=285/665), inaccuracies (49.40%, n=329/666), accountability challenges (45.20%, n=301/666), and data privacy risks (36.05%, n=239/663). Most respondents believed that peer reviewers require either some training (43.91%, n=310/706) or a lot of training (40.93%, n=289/706) to use GenAI chatbots effectively in peer review. Conclusion: Respondents reported perceived benefits of GenAI in peer review, alongside notable concerns regarding its use. While opinions were mixed, findings suggest both perceived utility and apprehension about potential risks. Further work is needed to understand these perspectives better and to explore how GenAI can be responsibly integrated into peer-review processes.

after.title: Preprint: Fentanyl dabbing with cannabis retail equipment: an ethnographic and drug-checking study
after.authors: Godvin, M.; Cecil, L.; Koncsol, A.; Molina, C. A.; Grabill, M.; Romero, R.; Jalayer, E.; Villanueva, N.; Arellano, O.; Cowan, A.; Buhr, R. G.; Englander, H.; Friedman, J. R.; Bourgois, P.; Shover, C. L.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Division of General Internal Medicine and Health Services Research, David Geffen School of Medicine, University of California, Los Angeles, Los Angeles, CA, USA
after.abstract: Background: Fentanyl's entrenchment in U.S. West Coast drug markets brought a shift from injecting to smoking illicit opioids. We characterize the next transition: the rise of 'dabbing,' vaporizing fentanyl with equipment sold for cannabis concentrates. Methods: This mixed-methods study combined ethnographic interviewing and participant observation among people who use fentanyl in California and Oregon (2024-2026) with survey data from a Los Angeles drug checking program. After identifying dabbing ethnographically, we added an optional smoking-method item to the survey. Results: Of 108 participants who stated a route of administration, 104 (96%) reported smoking; of 93 who named a smoking method, 81 (87%) reported dabbing. All 11 who first named another method and returned later then reported dabbing. Dabbing was reported at 250 of 405 (62%) encounters with a stated route. We observed participants adapting cannabis equipment. They praised dabbing's discretion, reduced stigma, and convenience, and its capacity for more large hits, more quickly; the same speed led some to call it wasteful, because it went through their fentanyl faster than other methods. Participants described rapidly rising tolerance and frequent dabbing-related burns, which we also observed. Some who had injected said dabbing approximated its "rush." Conclusions: Dabbing has become the dominant way to consume fentanyl among people using drug checking services in Los Angeles, and was observed in every other city where we did fieldwork. Clinicians and programs should ask people how they smoke fentanyl, not only whether they smoke or inject; dabbing may reduce some risks while increasing others.

after.title: Preprint: Digital cytometry of immune cell types from dried blood microsamples
after.authors: Ferry, Q. R.; Rajakumar, T.; Zeeck, M.; Chong-Morrison, V.; von Schrenck, T.; Ahmadi-Simab, K.; Steinkraus, B. R.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Muno GmbH, Hamburg, Germany
after.abstract: Enumeration of circulating immune cells is an established clinical practice implemented across a plethora of indications. While flow cytometry is the gold standard for this task, cellular deconvolution algorithms provide a robust computational alternative using molecular data. These digital cytometry pipelines typically rely on millilitre-scale venous blood samples. Here, we evaluated the potential of capillary blood microsampling as a patient-centric and minimally invasive approach for the digital cytometry of major lymphocyte populations (T cells, B cells, and natural killer cells; TBNK). In a cohort of 200 participants, we compared RNA sequencing based deconvolution performance between matched PAXgene-stabilised venous blood and Mitra capillary blood microsamples. While venous transcriptomes enabled highly accurate TBNK estimation, patient-matched capillary microsamples exhibited a significant reduction in deconvolution accuracy. Computational adaptations, including the integration of capillary-specific single-cell reference profiles, yielded only limited improvements. Instead, our analyses revealed that the performance deficit was primarily driven by the decreased transcriptome complexity of the capillary microsample libraries. This study highlights the critical role of transcript diversity for cellular deconvolution and reveals the current pre-analytical challenges that must be overcome to harness transcriptomics based digital cytometry using dried blood microsamples.

after.title: Preprint: Population-level indirect effects of HPV vaccination in high-income settings: a Bayesian modelling study
after.authors: Wang, R.; Jit, M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: New York University
after.abstract: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination provides direct protection to vaccinated individuals, but also indirectly protects unvaccinated individuals through reduced HPV transmission. Mechanistic transmission models that predict the magnitude of such effects have been crucial to informing vaccination strategies. However, nearly two decades of post-vaccination experience in high-income countries now allow us to empirically characterise how population-level indirect effects vary with vaccine coverage, time since vaccine introduction, and age. Methods We synthesised studies reporting HPV16/18 prevalence before and after vaccine introduction in high-income settings between 2007 and 2025. Indirect effects were estimated as the observed reduction in HPV16/18 prevalence after accounting for expected direct vaccine protection. We used a Bayesian hierarchical model to examine associations with vaccine coverage, time since vaccine introduction, and age at effect assessment across routine, catch-up, and non-targeted vaccination groups. XGBoost was used as a complementary, non-parametric approach. Findings Data from 11 high-income settings were included. Indirect effects increased during the first five to eight years after vaccine introduction and then remained relatively stable. Indirect effects generally decreased with increasing vaccine coverage. Patterns with age differed across vaccination groups. In the routine group, indirect effects increased during adolescence and remained positive at older observed ages. In the catch-up group, indirect effects decreased with age and approached zero or became negative after approximately age 25 years. XGBoost identified similar non-linear patterns. Interpretation Indirect protection against HPV16/18 develops gradually after vaccine introduction and varies with vaccine coverage, age, and vaccination group. This empirical approach can complement transmission models by using real-world evidence to characterise population-level indirect protection. However, making predictions outside the populations and ranges represented in the data should be done cautiously.

after.author_corresponding_institution: CDC
after.abstract: Importance: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of hospitalization in high-risk young children during their second RSV season. Nirsevimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody against RSV, is recommended for some children who are at increased risk for severe RSV and entering their second RSV season to prevent severe RSV disease. Because of limited eligibility criteria for second season nirsevimab, estimating its effectiveness is challenging. Objective: We evaluated nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations among young children eligible to receive nirsevimab during their second RSV season. Design: This retrospective case control study with a test-negative design was conducted during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 RSV seasons. Setting: Enrollment was in 26 hospitals across 24 U.S. states. Participants: Children eligible for nirsevimab during their second RSV season (as recommended in August 2023) were included. Nirsevimab-eligible children 8-23 months old hospitalized with respiratory symptoms were enrolled. Case-patients tested positive for RSV; control-patients tested negative for RSV. Exposures: Receipt of nirsevimab before or during the second RSV season and at least 7 days before symptom onset. Outcomes and measures: RSV-associated hospitalization. We estimated nirsevimab effectiveness using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, month and year of hospitalization, census region, and sex comparing the odds of second season nirsevimab receipt among case- and control-patients. Results: One hundred six case-patients and 125 control-patients were analyzed. Distributions of age, sex, race and ethnicity, and region were similar in case- and control-patients. Most case- and control-patients were eligible for nirsevimab because of chronic lung disease of prematurity (84.0% and 69.6%, respectively). Overall, 21 (19.8%) of case-patients and 53 (42.4%) of control-patients received nirsevimab. Adjusted nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 78.1% (95% CI, 55.2%-89.3%); the median interval from nirsevimab receipt to symptom onset was 66.5 days (IQR = 30-96 days). Effectiveness was estimated to be higher if nirsevimab was received 8-59 days before symptom onset (88.5%, 95% CI, 63.4%-96.4%). after.title: Preprint: Emergent Heterogeneity in Compartmental Disease Models
after.authors: Roswell, M.; Aghaeeyan, A.; Goel, T.; Beckett, S. J.; Weitz, J. S.; Dushoff, J.
after.author_corresponding_institution: McMaster University
after.abstract: Heterogeneity in infectious disease spread reshapes the risk and severity of outbreaks. This heterogeneity can arise from intrinsic individual-level differences in susceptibility, contact patterns, and infectious durations. Heterogeneity can also emerge from disease dynamics in a canonically homogeneous population, due to the fact that individuals randomly become infected at different times, recover after different intervals, and have access to different numbers of susceptible individuals. Here, we explore the mechanisms generating emergent heterogeneity by analyzing secondary case distributions within the SIR model. We show numerically and prove analytically that the variation in secondary cases, calculated over the course of the epidemic, does not change with R0. This is in contrast to the increasing variation in secondary cases in the linearized SIR model, often used to study heterogeneity at the beginning of an outbreak. When we consider forward cohorts of individuals infected at the same time, between-cohort variation increases as R0 increases, while within-cohort variation decreases. We show that these effects balance exactly, leading to the invariance of the variation in secondary cases with respect to R0. These results demonstrate the importance of considering emergent, as well as intrinsic, variation between individuals and of considering heterogeneity of transmission spread over the whole epidemic cycle, including substantive dynamical effects that appear even in the initial outbreak phase.

after.title: Preprint: Wastewater sequence data reveal national and cross-border virus transmission dynamics
after.authors: Odor, G.; Endler, L.; Amman, F.; Bergthaler, A.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Medical University of Vienna
after.abstract: Spatial epidemic models estimate disease transmission counts between populations using human mobility data, but location-to-location transmission is rarely observed directly. To address this gap, we develop mutation-counting methods to infer transmission structure from viral genetic variation measured in wastewater. In epidemic simulations with known transmission networks, our primary estimator robustly recovers spatial structure under realistic mutation-detection limits. Applied to spatiotemporal SARS-CoV-2 wastewater data from Austria, the method reveals strong seasonal reorganization, with inferred transmission becoming more geographically localized in winter and more dispersed in summer. We further identify locations with systematically higher or lower connectivity than expected from commuting, with temporal changes coinciding with regional restrictions, reopening and tourism. We then test whether such inference remains possible across national borders, recovering coherent spatial structure and temporal variation in connectivity between Austria, Switzerland and Liechtenstein. These results establish wastewater sequence data as a promising complement to mobility data for monitoring spatial transmission and detecting changes in epidemic spread associated with seasonality and interventions.

after.title: Preprint: Evaluation of out-of-hospital management of asthma attacks prior to consultation at the paediatric emergency department in Martinique
after.authors: Julia, A.; Denis, J.
after.author_corresponding_institution: CHU Martinique
after.abstract: Background: Asthma is a chronic, multifactorial disease that progresses in episodes and requires effective coordination of care between healthcare professionals and patients. Objective: To describe and evaluate pre-hospital therapeutic management of asthma attacks. Methods: Cross-sectional, prospective, single-centre, observational and descriptive study of patients consulting for asthma attacks at the Fort de France paediatric emergency department between July and November 2024. All patients included were children between the ages of 1 and 18 who had already been diagnosed with asthma by a doctor and who presented to the emergency department for an asthma attack. Several other parameters were assessed, such as the parents' perception of the emergency situation, the child's asthma control in the month prior to the attack, the child's usual medical follow-up, and their usual treatment. Results: 175 patients were included in the study. Eight patients were excluded from the study because their questionnaire had a response rate of less than 50%. Of the 175 patients included, only 6.7% received perfect pre-hospital care, 29.3% received good quality care, 36% received moderate quality care, and 10.3% received poor quality care before arriving at the emergency department. (17.7% did not complete all the items necessary to calculate the score). 11.6% of children did not receive treatment before consulting the emergency department. Among the 88.9% who took short-acting {beta}2 agonists, only 52% received at least 3 series and 66.2% were given doses appropriate for their weight. 21.6% received oral corticosteroids before arriving at the emergency department. Conclusions: The management of asthma attacks outside of hospital settings is not optimal for a large proportion of patients in the study. Several areas for improvement have been identified and require joint action by healthcare professionals.

after.title: Preprint: Bipolar Disorder and Education: Deciphering a Complex Relationship using Genetic and Sibling Differences in a Multi-cohort Study
after.authors: K Madhavan, V.; Demange, P. A.; Ayorech, Z.; Hottenga, J. J.; Bartels, M.; Ystrom, E.; Nivard, M. G.; Akingbuwa, W. A.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
after.abstract: Background. While bipolar disorder has a positive genetic correlation (r~0.3) with educational attainment (EA), individuals with bipolar disorder diagnoses have lower EA in adulthood. To clarify this paradox, we hypothesise that bipolar disorder and educational outcomes share a positive genetic association, reflected in high academic performance earlier in life, but that emerging bipolar disorder symptoms disrupt academic trajectories, leading to the observed poor long-term educational outcomes. Methods. We employed a sibling comparison design across four population-based cohorts (Ntotal = 1,145,795 siblings). First, we tested the association between bipolar disorder polygenic scores (PGS) and educational outcomes (EA and academic performance) in the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study (MoBa) and UK Biobank (UKB). Second, we examined associations between academic performance at ages 10, 12, 13, and 14 and subsequent bipolar disorder diagnosis using registry data from Statistics Netherlands and Statistics Norway (with the Norwegian Control and Payment of Health Reimbursements Databases). Findings. Siblings with higher bipolar disorder PGS had significantly higher EA ({beta}W = 0.03, 95% CI [0.01, 0.05], N=16,746) as well as higher academic performance at age 10 (0.03 [0.01, 0.05], N=17,677) in MoBa. Secondly, individuals with bipolar disorder had better overall academic performance than their unaffected sibling at ages 10 (HRW = 1.12 [1.02, 1.22], N=343,898) and 12 (1.59 [1.16, 2.19], N=619,796). However, individuals with bipolar disorder experienced a decline in academic performance at ages 13 (0.84 [0.73, 0.96], N=320,342) and 14 (0.72 [0.61, 0.85], N=299,039). Interpretation. Bipolar disorder shares a positive genetic association with educational outcomes, reflected in early academic advantage. This is followed by an academic decline in mid-adolescence, highlighting the period of educational disruption associated with bipolar disorder. Funding. The Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Sciences, European Research Council, the Research Council of Norway, the Swedish Research Council

after.title: Preprint: Chatbot as an intervention on physical activity: A systematic review and meta-analysis with meta-regression
after.authors: Fu, L.; Song, D.; Bai, Y.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Utah
after.abstract: Background: Chatbots offer scalable, accessible, and personalized support for physical activity (PA). This review synthesized evidence on their efficacy and examined potential moderators. Methods: Eleven databases were searched for English-language published through January 27, 2026. Eligibility was assessed using the PICOS framework. Data extraction was guided by the research questions, mERA checklist, and PRISMA 2020. Risk of bias was evaluated using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and the NIH Quality Assessment Tool. Meta-analyses reported Hedges' g. Publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots, Egger's regression, and trim-and-fill analyses. Potential moderators were examined through subgroup analyses and meta-regression. Results: A total of 12,481 records were identified, of which 43 studies were included in the systematic review and 27 in the meta-analysis. Most studies included in the meta-analysis had some risk-of-bias concerns (16/27). Chatbot interventions produced a significant small-to-moderate post-intervention effect on PA (g = 0.31, 95% CI [0.19, 0.44]; n = 24), whereas the follow-up effect was small and non-significant (g = 0.11, 95% CI [-0.01, 0.22]; n = 4). Effects varied across PA outcomes (g = 0.08-0.44), and several subgroup differences helped explain the significant heterogeneity. For daily steps, significant subgroup differences were observed by clinical status, while intervention duration (QM = 6.09, p = 0.048) and clinical status (QM = 5.69, p = 0.017) were significant moderators. Conclusions: Chatbot interventions showed small-to-moderate post-intervention effects but limited follow-up effects. Few significant moderators were identified, underscoring the need for more rigorous RCTs.
